facts.raw_span: 2 days of left orbital pain
hypertension controlled with lisinopril
several months of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis
Visual acuity: 20/25 OD and 20/400 OS
Edematous, hyperemic left eyelids
Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye
Normal intraocular pressure
Normal fundi on both sides
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding largely limited to the extraconal space
Initial cultures isolated gram-positive cocci in chains; later identified as pan-susceptible Streptococcus pyogenes
Increased abscess size with globe compression
diffusion-weighted imaging showed acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve

concepts.why: The patient has a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding and increased abscess size with globe compression.
The patient has edematous, hyperemic left eyelids, diffuse limitation in extraocular movements, and a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess.
The patient has acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve as shown by diffusion-weighted imaging.
The patient has several months of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis.
The patient has initial cultures isolated gram-positive cocci in chains, later identified as pan-susceptible Streptococcus pyogenes.

rationales.F01: Left orbital pain is consistent with lacrimal sac abscess and orbital cellulitis.
rationales.F02: Hypertension is not directly related to the presented symptoms.
rationales.F03: Epiphora is a symptom that can be associated with lacrimal sac abscess and epiphora itself.
rationales.F04: Visual acuity decrease in the left eye suggests an issue affecting the eye, such as lacrimal sac abscess, orbital cellulitis, or optic nerve injury.
rationales.F05: Edematous and hyperemic left eyelids are consistent with lacrimal sac abscess and orbital cellulitis.
rationales.F06: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye suggests an issue affecting the eye or surrounding tissues, such as lacrimal sac abscess, orbital cellulitis, or optic nerve injury.
rationales.F07: Normal intraocular pressure does not specifically rule in or out any of the considered conditions.
rationales.F08: Normal fundi on both sides do not specifically rule in or out any of the considered conditions.
rationales.F09: Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding is highly suggestive of lacrimal sac abscess.
rationales.F10: Gram-positive cocci in chains, later identified as pan-susceptible Streptococcus pyogenes, suggest a streptococcal infection.
rationales.F11: Increased abscess size with globe compression suggests progression of the lacrimal sac abscess and potential impact on surrounding structures.
rationales.F12: Diffusion-weighted imaging showing acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve is highly suggestive of optic nerve injury.
